column1: // This document describes the DSL for the specification of an SPL.
// Version 1.0, June 1, 2024, by Yannis HÅbenthal & Ulrich Eisenecker
// A comment begins with // and must be followed by a whitespace (space, tab).
// It extends to the next newline character.
// Keywords are
// SPL, FEATURES, CATEGORIES, END, MAX_RANK,
// EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES, MISSING_SYSTEMS and
// AVAILABLE_SYSTEMS.
// A keyword must be terminated with a whitespace.
// Keywords are NOT case sensitive.
// SPL has the cardinality 0..1.
// It enables the specification of a name for a DSL.
// The name must not contain any whitespaces.
// A name is terminated by a whitespace.
SPL
// FEATURES has the cardinality 1.
// It specifies the number of independent features of an SPL,
// followed by the names of the independent features.
// There must be exactly as many feature names as the number of features specified.
// A number is terminated by any character that cannot be part of an integer,
// e.g. a whitespace.
// IMPORTANT: The list of feature names is NOT terminated with END.
// Currently, there is no check for duplicate feature names.
FEATURES
Factorial_Calculation
column2: // This serves as as a parent feature of an xor-feature group

column1: Iterative_Factorial_Calculation
Recursive_Factorial_Calculation
Logging
Arithmetic_Checking
// CATEGORIES has the cardinality 0..1.
// CATEGORIES is used to define which feature categories are
// to be included in the feature analysis and feature isolation.
// Valid category values are F, A, O, AN, ON, ANF and ONF.
// If CATEGORY is not explicitly specified, F is implicitly assumed
// to be the only category. The category values can be specified
// in any order. If a category value is specified more than once,
// CATEGORY can appear anywhere in the SPL specification.
CATEGORIES
F
A
O
N
AN
ON
ANF
ONF
END
// MAX_RANK has the cardinality 0..1.
// It specifies the maximum number of feature interactions
// in relation to the categories A, O, AN, ON, ANF and ONF
// that are taken into account. MAX_RANK must be equal to
// or less than the number of independent features.
// FEATURES must be specified before MAX_RANK.
MAX_RANK
// EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES has the cardinality 0..1.
// It is used to explicitly specify dependent features.
// Possible dependencies are REQUIRES and EXCLUDES.
// A feature must be specified by its name introduced in the
// FEATURES specification, which must precede it for this
// reason. It is only possible to specify a dependency
// between exactly two features, with one exception.
// If a feature is specified as requiring itself,
// e.g. feature_a requires feature_a,
// this means that this feature must be contained in
// every system of an SPL, i.e. it becomes a so-called
// core feature. After the parsing of the SPL specification
// is completed, a SAT solver is executed to check the
// specified dependencies for consistency, also with
// regard to any specified available or missing systems.
// The list of explicit dependencies must be concluded with
//  END. If EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES is missing,
// there are no explicitly dependent features.
/EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES
Factorial_Calculation
Iterative_Factorial_Calculation
Recursive_Factorial_Calculation
Iterative_Factorial_Calculation
END

column1: // General remarks
// The keywords SPL and CATEGORIES-END can appear in any order.
// If CATEGORIES-END is missing, only independent features will be considered.
// If EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES-END is missing, then there are no explicitly dependent features.
// Either MISSING_SYSTEMS-END or AVAILABLE_SYSTEMS-END can be specified.
// If none of them is specified, all possible systems will be considered.
// The items of CATEGORIES-END, EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES-END,
// MISSING_SYSTEMS-END and AVAILABLE_SYSTEMS-END can appear in any order.
// FEATURES must be specified before EXPLICIT_DEPENDENCIES, MISSING_SYSTEMS and AVAILABLE_SYSTEMS.
// Keywords are not case-sensitive. The names of independent feature are case-sensitive.
